tests_pass_but_would_not_catch: src/lib/reportsExecutive.test.js (33 green) is a PURE-FUNCTION oracle. It cannot see the payload shape at all: an SQL body that returns the right numbers under the wrong chart contract — exactly blockers B1/B2/B3 — passes every one of these tests. All three were found by reading ChartCard.jsx against the live payload, not by a test.

No test in the repo asserts the ScatterBody series-pair contract. ChartCard.test.jsx exists but the tab tests mock recharts (§2ב C6), so a scatter with a missing Y column renders 'fine' in jsdom. The same class already shipped once in report_m16 (F2). A real guard would be a lint-style assertion over every payload: type==='scatter' => series.length===2 && data[0] has both keys.

`discountTierOf` tests lock the tier boundaries, and the SQL repeats them as a `case` expression. Nothing compares the two: a typo in the SQL (`d < 5` instead of `d <= 5`) would keep the JS tests green and move 5%-discount quotes to the wrong tier. Only the baseline comparison (353/301/125/58) catches it — and only while those numbers stay current.

`buildRatioHistogram` and the SQL `values` list are two independent copies of the same 8 buckets. The new `ratioBucketLabelFor` test pins the JS side; the SQL side is pinned only by the live equality of the 8 counts to the card.
meta.sort / customer_filter_ignored / drill_echo have no test anywhere — they are contract keys read by ReportSurface, and their absence is silent (the fallback quietly produces the wrong aria-sort).
